div.l: Anon to draw eủery wight beganne
And shortly to tellen as it was
Were it bi auenture chaunce or cas
The sothe is this the cutte fil to þᵉ kniȝt
Of which ful glad and blithe was eủery wiȝt
And telle he must his tale as was resou
By forwarde and by Composiciou
As ye han herd what nedith wurdꝭes mo
And whan this good man sie þᵗat it was so
As he that wise was and obedient
To kepe his forward by free assent
He seid syn I shal begynne the game
What welcum be the cutte in goddis name
Now lat us ride and herkneth what I seye
And wᵗith that wurd we riden furth our wey
And he began with right a mery chere
His tale anon . and seid as ye may here
The prolog of the knightꝭes tale
Whilom as olde Stories tellen̄ vs
Ther was a Duke þat hight Theseus
Of Athenes he was lord ⁊and goủernour͗e
And in his time such a Conquerour͗e
That grett̉er was ther none vnd̉er the Sūnne
Ful many a riche cuntre had he wūnne
What with his wisdom and his chiualry
He conquerd all the Ream of Feminy
That whilom was clepid Scithia
And weddid the Quene Ipolita
And brought hir home wᵗith him to hˢis cūntr͗e
With much glorie and gret solempnite
And eke hir yong sustir͗e Emelie
And thus with victorie ⁊and wᵗith melodie
Lete I this noble Duke to Athenes ride
And al his host in armes him beside
And certis if it nere to long to here
I wold haue told you fulli the maner͗e
Hou wonne was the Ream of Feminy
By Theseus and his Cheualry
